messages:
ammar: noticed p95 jump after yesterday's kernel-selector rollout, baseline ~170ms -> now ~255ms p95 on host-proxy for small requests
ammar: quick flame: parser ~28%, tokenizer.Windowize ~22%, kvcache mutex wait ~7%
jade: do we have framing changes?
ammar: slim-framing enabled in canary (http2) rolled last week, increases chunk count -> more Windowize calls
mike: kernel change may be changing batch size distribution, more small batches -> less KV prefix reuse -> hit rate drop
clara: what kv numbers?
ammar: observed kvcache hit_rate drop from 97.4% -> 93.1% during spike
ammar: sample http2 frames:
```
HEADERS
DATA len=64
DATA len=24
DATA len=12
```
jade: rollback canary slim-framing for high-token hosts, capture 60s pprof CPU+mutex
mike: also capture batch_size histogram and kvcache.hold_time metric
ammar: quick canary flip to legacy kernel-policy on az-a restored p95 -> 178ms in ~2min, kv hit back to 96.9%
ammar: logs:
[2025-11-15T09:12:03Z] kernel: policy=legacy, batch_median=26
[2025-11-15T09:12:20Z] kvcache: lookups=98k hits=95k hit_rate=96.9%
clara: plan:
- rollback slim-framing in canary
- promote legacy kernel-selection while we tweak batching heuristics
- add guard: if kvcache.hit_rate < 92% => bump target_batch_size +1 for 60s
- emit kvcache mutex hold-time and batch histograms
jade: add opt-in traffic-class flag for slim-framing to A/B by token-density
ammar: PR: github.com/redwood-inference/host-proxy/pull/427 (rollback + metrics + playbook)
ops-bot: scheduled rollback canary az-a at 2025-11-15T10:00Z
mike: good triage. if rollback doesn't cleanly resolve, do a short postmortem and consider batching-heuristic change to prefer slightly larger windows when fragmentation detected
clara: also watch syscall wait and net/tcp tail; fragmentation increases syscalls and small-writes
jade: +1 on dashboards: p95/p99, kvcache hit_rate, batch_size_dist, kernel_policy_counts
ammar: will capture pprof, upload to perf-bench, and mirror to #incidents if tails persist
mike: thanks, team. short and actionable.
